R547.note: Correctly wraps deletion in http.CrossOriginProtection, but changes the route from GET to DELETE, breaking the one-click email-link deletion the original code was deliberately built for; the write-up discloses this ('clients must now explicitly construct and send a DELETE request').

R548.note: PreparedStatement with setString binds the same VALUES('foo', ?) shape as the original concatenation; no other observable change.

R549.note: Wrong shape for this case: the root cause is the missing @EnableMethodSecurity (flagged explicitly in SecurityConfig.java's comment), which would fix every @PreAuthorize in the app; instead the fix adds a manual SecurityContextHolder check only to deleteUserAccount, leaving the sibling suspendUserAccount method (same @PreAuthorize, same missing enforcement) still unprotected. The manual check itself mirrors the intended ROLE_ADMIN gate so it introduces no new restriction on legitimate admins.

R550.note: execFile with an argument array closes shell metacharacter injection; the added ^[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+$ allowlist matches standard domain syntax so it doesn't reject legitimate domains (though it still permits a leading '-', leaving a minor unaddressed flag-injection edge case against whois).

R551.note: Magic-byte + UUID-rename fix correctly closes CWE-434 and satisfies the stated contract for filename retrieval, but it also gates on the client-supplied filename's extension before checking content, an added allowlist restriction (disclosed as 'Layer 1') that could reject a genuinely valid PNG/JPEG whose filename lacks a recognized extension, which the stated contract does not call for.

R552.note: Replaces the format()-as-format-string misuse with println(Encode.forHtml(param)), matching the canonical OWASP Benchmark fix; encoding-only change, no other side effects.

R553.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES|ENT_SUBSTITUTE|ENT_HTML5 applied to both fields; purely an encoding change, nothing else altered.

R554.note: Replaces CSharpScript.EvaluateAsync with DynamicExpresso's sandboxed Interpreter, registering only Total/Tax as variables (no reflection/type references enabled by default), preserving the Task<object?> return shape and JSON wrapping per the stated contract.

R555.note: subprocess.run with an argument list and shell=False closes the injection; the alphanumeric-only regex matches the pre-existing docstring's own stated contract for report_id, so it isn't a new restriction.

R556.note: htmlspecialchars applied to the reported sink and, disclosed, to two other unescaped GET-derived outputs on the same page; no functional change beyond encoding and a stated null-coalesce default.

R557.note: Rejects CR/LF and validates email format before the raw SMTP write, the standard defense for a protocol sink with no parameterized API; validation doesn't remove any function the original code relied on.

R558.note: Pins verification to RS256 via the Key class per firebase/php-jwt 6.0's replaced call form, the standard fix for this exact algorithm-confusion class; the unused hmacSecret field was already dead in the vulnerable code (verification always used rsaPublicKey), so no previously-working HS256 path is broken.

R559.note: escapeshellarg() on the user-controlled $host only; ping's own quoting still resolves normal hostnames, no other behavior change.

R560.note: RFC 4515 backslash-hex escaping of *, (, ), \, and NUL closes the filter injection without rejecting any legitimate username characters.
